sources.entry: AirPoise - Menu bar app that uses AirPods motion sensors for head-posture reminders and configurable head-gesture shortcuts.

summary.one_liner: AirPoise is a macOS menu-bar app that uses the motion sensors in compatible AirPods to give head-posture reminders and run actions from head gestures like nods, shakes, and tilts.
summary.what_it_does: AirPoise reads head-pose data from AirPods Pro, 3, 4, Max, or Beats Fit Pro (set as the Mac's sound output) at about 25 samples per second. It has two functions: a posture coach that reminds you when your chin drifts forward or your head tilts, and head-gesture shortcuts. The shortcuts can be bound to 16 gestures such as nod, double nod, shake, look left/right/up/down, tilt, hold-tilt, lean, and roll. Each gesture can trigger a keyboard shortcut, an Apple Shortcuts entry, a URL or app, media/volume/brightness controls, Mission Control or Spaces, a notification, spoken text, or a user-written shell or AppleScript command. Sensitivity, cooldown, and hold duration are adjustable, and posture thresholds and reminder style (overlay, notification, sound, or speech) are configurable. The README says it needs no camera, account, or internet, and uploads nothing.
use_cases: reminder to sit up straight while working
control music playback with head nods
switch macOS desktops or Spaces by glancing
trigger Mission Control with a head tilt
how_to_run: Install from the AirPoise-1.0.0.dmg by dragging the app to Applications (or build from source)
Put on compatible AirPods and set them as the Mac's sound output
Click Calibrate upright while sitting the way you want to sit
git clone the repository and run ./scripts/build-app.sh
stack: AppKit (menu bar UI, implied by AppKit-free AirPoiseCore module)
notable: Uses the AirPods motion sensors already used for Spatial Audio, so no camera is needed
Gesture actions can be bound to keyboard shortcuts, Apple Shortcuts, URLs, apps, media keys, and system functions
Posture coach ignores tracking while walking
Core logic is separated into an AppKit-free module with unit tests
caveats: Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later and AirPods with head tracking; original AirPods and AirPods 2 do not work
Sees head pose only, not full spine posture
Intel Macs on Sonoma may run, but only Apple Silicon is tested
Custom keyboard shortcuts need Accessibility permission
